name: Citation Graphs Over Time
title: Citation Graphs Over Time
answer: Citation graphs over time map how research papers cite one another across years, showing influence, emergence, and decay of ideas. This site's library of 135 research papers and 10,555 extracted claims provides a small but structured base for tracing such links. The scope covers directed edges from citing work to cited work, with timestamps from publication dates, and includes books, models, tools, and glossary terms as nodes where relevant. It does not cover non-scholarly web links or social media mentions.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The graphs are built from bibliographic records and full text where available, stored as nodes and edges with year attributes. Computation runs on standard graph databases or in memory for the site's current scale, which is modest compared to large academic indexes. The site links to original papers rather than to the Consensus search tool, so edge resolution depends on persistent identifiers such as DOIs and arXiv IDs. No special hardware is required for this size.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work begins by parsing reference lists and matching them to known papers in the library, then extracting claims to weight edges by shared concepts. Temporal analysis uses snapshots by year, cumulative degree, and simple path length measures rather than deep learning. The 10,555 claims allow a lightweight semantic layer, but the core method is graph traversal and counting. Researchers typically inspect clusters and bursts manually.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on bibliographic accuracy and provenance. Because the site links to original papers, broken links and version mismatches are the main operational risk, not copyright of citation data itself. Citation graphs can encode prestige bias and self citation, so the site should record edge provenance and not silently merge duplicate records. No personal data is involved beyond author names, which are public.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Where it is going is toward richer temporal models that distinguish direct influence from background citation norms. The site's 801 models and 732 tools could be linked into the graph as citing or cited artifacts, expanding beyond papers. Future work may add field normalized citation counts and decay curves, but only if the underlying paper metadata remains clean. The constraint of linking to originals rather than a search tool keeps the graph auditable.
